podcast.title: British Singer, Songwriter, and Model
podcast.body: Bakar, whose full name is Abu Bakar Shariff, is a British artist known for his roles as a singer, songwriter, and model. "He's a British singer, songwriter and model, interesting resume, and he has a rep for an experimental sort of indie rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career on SoundCloud
podcast.body: His musical journey began by anonymously uploading tracks to SoundCloud, establishing his experimental indie rock style. "His career began by uploading tracks anonymously to SoundCloud."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Genre-Blurring Approach
podcast.body: Bakar's musical style intentionally blurs the lines between rap, indie rock, rock, and various other genres, an approach compared to Bloc Party. "Since then, his whole thing has been to blur the lines between rap, indie rock, rock, and any number of other genres. In some senses, he's doing a lot of the same sort of thing as Block Party."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Yemeni and Tanzanian Heritage
podcast.body: Bakar's parents are of Yemeni and Tanzanian descent, and he grew up in Camden, North London. "Mom and Dad were Yemeni and Tanzanian, but he grew up in Camden in North London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: SoundCloud Origins
xref.body: KennyHoopla, like Bakar, began his career by posting his music to SoundCloud, achieving significant early success with his track "Cave." "He started by posting stuff to Sam Cloud, and one of the songs was called Cave. It became the most streamed song of all time on Sam Cloud."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
